topics.title: What development promises: different people, different goals

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why persons in different life situations have different developmental goals.
Recognise that what is development for one person may be harmful for another.
Identify non-material goals such as equal treatment, freedom, security and respect alongside income.
Explain that people look at a mix of income and non-income goals when making choices.
Explain that notions of national development differ and must be judged by fairness and how many people benefit.

topics.title: Comparing countries and states: per capita income and averages
topics.ncert_sections: How to compare different countries or states?; Average income

concepts.learning_objective: Define per capita income and explain why it is used to compare countries.
State the World Bank's criterion for classifying countries.
Calculate averages and explain why they can hide disparities in distribution.

topics.title: Income and other criteria; public facilities
topics.ncert_sections: Income and other criteria; Public facilities

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret infant mortality rate, literacy rate and net attendance ratio to compare states.
Explain why collective provision of health, education and PDS improves well-being.
State the criteria the UNDP's Human Development Report uses to compare countries.
Interpret Human Development Report data comparing India with its neighbours.
Distinguish renewable from non-renewable resources with examples such as groundwater and crude oil.
Explain why development must be sustainable for future generations.
